solutions.check: grid and clues read from the FT's printable PDF, its numbering matching the clue list; every fifteensquared answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: French preposition in spoken test

indicators.note: the French word is placed inside the word for spoken, as the clue says one sits in the other

parts.note: spoken means oral, said rather than written
de is the French preposition meaning of or from

explanation.surface: A French grammar point crops up in an oral examination.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spoken test' looks like one unit meaning an oral exam, but 'spoken' alone gives ORAL and 'test' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A severe trial or testing experience is a classic synonym here.

clue.text: Meat producer taking game for two universities

parts.note: an ox is an animal raised for beef
bridge is a card game

explanation.surface: A cattle farmer takes up cards and lands at two famous colleges.
explanation.definitionFit: A blend of Oxford and Cambridge, used for the two ancient English universities together.

clue.text: Collected tales of French-English PM

parts.note: de is French for of
David Cameron was a British Prime Minister

explanation.surface: A book of stories by a Franco-British premier.
explanation.definitionFit: Boccaccio's collection of a hundred stories told over ten days.

clue.text: Keys admit private secretary to part of the church

indicators.note: admitting lets something in, so the secretary goes inside the keys

parts.note: A and E are two musical keys
PS stands for private secretary

explanation.surface: Someone with keys lets an assistant into a section of the church.
explanation.definitionFit: The semicircular recess at the east end of a church.

clue.text: Less familiar route followed by US commando

indicators.note: the route word comes first and the commando word follows it in the answer

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for street, a route
a Ranger is a member of a US Army commando unit

explanation.surface: An unfamiliar path is taken, with an American special-forces soldier trailing behind.
explanation.definitionFit: Comparative of strange, meaning more unknown or unfamiliar.

clue.text: A climbing frame put in the nursery, perhaps

definitions.text: A climbing frame put in the nursery, perhaps

parts.words: A climbing frame put in the nursery, perhaps
parts.note: the climbing frame is not for children but for plants, and the nursery is a garden centre

explanation.surface: Play equipment installed in a child's room.
explanation.definitionFit: A lattice of wood that climbing plants grow up, as sold at plant nurseries.

clue.text: It provides opportunities for advanced theatrical work

definitions.text: It provides opportunities for advanced theatrical work

parts.words: It provides opportunities for advanced theatrical work
parts.note: advanced means placed forward, the part of a theatre platform jutting in front of the curtain

explanation.surface: Something that offers chances for experienced actors.
explanation.definitionFit: The area of a stage projecting in front of the proscenium arch, nearer the audience.

clue.text: Enormous soldier — a six-footer

parts.note: GI is an American soldier
an ant has six legs, so it is a six-footer

explanation.surface: A huge soldier who stands six feet tall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Six-footer' looks like a tall person, but it means a creature with six feet.
explanation.definitionFit: Used as an adjective, it means huge or of great size.

clue.text: A trying delay

parts.note: trying in the legal sense: the delay before an accused is put on trial, held in custody or on bail

explanation.surface: An irritating hold-up.
explanation.definitionFit: Committal of an accused person to custody or bail while awaiting trial.

clue.text: They sit for qualifications

definitions.meaning: people who sit on horses or bikes
clauses added to a document or statement that qualify it

explanation.surface: Candidates sitting exams to earn certificates.
explanation.definitionFit: They are both horsemen sitting in the saddle and added provisos to a bill.

clue.text: Lapse into bad habits, being left in rear

indicators.note: the clue says the left letter is placed in the word for rear

parts.note: the backside is the rear or bottom

explanation.surface: Someone falls back into old vices after being left at the back.
explanation.definitionFit: To relapse into former bad behaviour is the standard meaning of the phrasal verb.

clue.text: It's true the head of the monarchy has it

definitions.text: It's true the head of the monarchy has it

parts.note: real means true or genuine

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter, here taken from monarchy

explanation.surface: A claim that a king or queen genuinely possesses something.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition too: a realm is the kingdom that a monarch holds.
explanation.definitionFit: A kingdom is the domain that belongs to the ruler, so it is what the monarchy possesses.

clue.text: A foot doctor is after a first-class return

indicators.note: the doctor's letters come after the reversed first-class piece
a return comes back, so the first-class term is read backwards

parts.note: A1 is first-class, written here as AI
MB is a Bachelor of Medicine, a doctor

explanation.surface: A podiatrist follows on from a premium-fare journey home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Foot' is the poetic metrical unit, not the body part a doctor might treat.
explanation.definitionFit: In prosody, an unstressed then stressed syllable makes this metrical foot.

clue.text: Capital way to serve beef tender-loin

definitions.meaning: the capital city of New Zealand
beef fillet wrapped in pastry is a famous dish named after the Duke

explanation.surface: A good way of cooking a cut of beef.
explanation.definitionFit: It is both New Zealand's capital and the name of a dish of fillet in pastry.

clue.text: Reach the others and stop

definitions.meaning: to arrive at the rest, the others

explanation.surface: Catching up with the group and halting.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to stop moving, and literally reads as arriving at the remainder.

clue.text: Ugly sisters refused a drink, taken aback by stepmother at first

indicators.note: taken aback suggests going backwards, so the refusal and drink are read in reverse

parts.note: refused means no
grog is a drink, rum and water

indicators.note: at first takes the first letter of stepmother

explanation.surface: Cinderella's ugly sisters are denied a drink and startled by their stepmother.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface points to the Cinderella pantomime, but the ugly sisters are the mythical snake-haired trio.
explanation.definitionFit: Mythical sisters, like Medusa, so hideous that a glance turned onlookers to stone.

clue.text: Attacks, throwing stones

indicators.note: throwing in the sense of throwing into disorder signals rearranging the letters

explanation.surface: Assaults carried out by hurling rocks.
explanation.definitionFit: To set on someone is to attack them; the third-person form matches.

clue.text: Raise cost somehow, or get cut off

indicators.note: somehow says the letters come together in some other way, an anagram

explanation.surface: Put prices up or be shunned by customers.
explanation.definitionFit: To exclude someone from a group is to cut them off socially.

clue.text: Case of foreign wine sent up to college-head

parts.note: the head, or first letter, of college is C

indicators.note: in a down entry, sent up means the wine is written upwards, backwards

parts.note: retsina is a Greek wine

explanation.surface: A crate of imported wine dispatched to the master of a college.
explanation.definitionFit: A metal container for storing food or tea is a kind of case.

clue.text: Insert a new form of word for "buries"

indicators.note: making a new form of the word means rearranging its letters

explanation.surface: An instruction to rework a word into a synonym for burying.
explanation.definitionFit: To inter a body is to bury it, so this form means buries.

clue.text: New Orleans is in Italy!

indicators.note: new suggests a fresh version, so the city's letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A geographical howler placing the American city in Italy.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines as well: a new arrangement of Orleans is indeed a city in Italy.
explanation.definitionFit: A port city on the south-west coast of Italy, scene of 1943 Allied landings.

clue.text: A target set for crafty rivals

indicators.note: set in the sense of arranged signals the letters being put in a new order

explanation.surface: A goal is fixed for cunning competitors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crafty' is punning on craft, boats: the rivals are crews.
explanation.definitionFit: A boat race meeting is an event held for competing vessels, or craft.

clue.text: One's getting in support to carry on the fight

indicators.note: getting in means entering, so one's goes inside the support

parts.note: a rest is a support
one is I, with 's giving IS

explanation.surface: One fighter gets back up with help to continue battling.
explanation.definitionFit: To keep opposing or fighting against something is to withstand it.

clue.text: Representations will be made if game is disrupted

indicators.note: disrupted means thrown into disorder, so the letters are shuffled

explanation.surface: Pictures will be produced if a match is interrupted.
explanation.definitionFit: Pictures or likenesses are representations of things.

clue.text: Still awaiting a formal proposal?

definitions.meaning: without a motion, the formal proposal at a meeting

explanation.surface: A meeting stalled because no one has tabled anything.
explanation.definitionFit: Being completely stationary is the plain sense; the second reading is a pun.

clue.text: Writer Kipling never expected to meet

definitions.meaning: Kipling's line says East and West are two, and never shall meet

explanation.surface: An author whom Kipling never thought he'd come across.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the pen name of Samuel Clemens and an old word meaning two.

clue.text: Mail goes astray in the country

indicators.note: going astray means wandering off course, so the letters wander into a new order

explanation.surface: Post gets lost somewhere in rural parts.
explanation.definitionFit: A landlocked West African nation.

clue.text: Old ship with a right to proceed

parts.note: to go is to proceed

explanation.surface: An ancient vessel is given permission to sail.
explanation.definitionFit: Jason sailed this legendary vessel in Greek myth.

clue.text: Brush and feed

definitions.meaning: to brush is to touch lightly in passing
to feed on grass, as cattle do

explanation.surface: Grooming and nourishing an animal.
explanation.definitionFit: It means both a light skimming touch and animals eating in a field.

clue.text: Reserve having to practise while the others go out

indicators.note: the others going out means they stand outside the practise word

parts.note: the rest means the others
to train is to practise

explanation.surface: One person stays back to train while everyone else heads off.
explanation.definitionFit: Reserve in the sense of self-control or holding back is a synonym.

clue.text: Ratification contains error

indicators.note: an error suggests the letters are got wrong, mixed up into another order

explanation.surface: An official approval document has a mistake in it.
explanation.definitionFit: Formal approval or authorisation is one meaning of the word.

clue.text: A Peeping Tom? You've to reform, right?

indicators.note: reforming means reshaping, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A snooper is told it's time to change his ways.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who gets pleasure from secretly watching others is a peeper.
